children: Disc Medicine reported initial Phase 2 RESTORE-PV data showing DISC-3405 controlled hematocrit and markedly reduced phlebotomy events.
Phase 2 RESTORE-PV enrolled 40 PV patients (20 Cohort A, 20 Cohort B); efficacy reported for Cohort A, safety for both cohorts.
Cohort A (n=13 completers at 26 weeks): mean phlebotomies fell from 4.0 to 0.6 in 26 weeks (p<0.0001); 61.5% remained phlebotomy-free.
Mean hematocrit was maintained <45% through week 26 in Cohort A, with initial improvement in symptom burden.
Pharmacodynamics in Cohort A showed dose-proportional PK, increased hepcidin, reduced serum iron and increased ferritin.
DISC-3405 was generally well-tolerated across cohorts; adverse events aligned with disease and injection reactions were mild and self-limited.

title: Disc Medicine shows DISC-3405 reduces phlebotomy, controls hematocrit in RESTORE-PV Phase 2
